sdsc-ordes/tripsu.notes: Time-to-close considers *all* closed PRs — merged + declined. Differs from ``cr_duration`` which is acceptance-speed only. A wide gap between the two means the project closes-without-merging slowly.

sdsc-ordes/tripsu.name: Upstream Code Dependencies
sdsc-ordes/tripsu.question: What does this project build on?
sdsc-ordes/tripsu.description: Count of distinct upstream repositories this project depends on, resolved from its dependency manifests into the Neo4j `DEPENDS_ON` graph.
sdsc-ordes/tripsu.label: direct upstream dependencies
sdsc-ordes/tripsu.unification: Single Cypher ``count(DISTINCT dep)`` over outbound ``DEPENDS_ON`` edges from the repo node.
sdsc-ordes/tripsu.notes: Counts distinct outbound ``DEPENDS_ON`` edges resolved to concrete upstream repositories. Reflects what the crawler resolved from dependency manifests — unresolved / private packages aren't edges, so this is a floor, not the full lock-file count. Edge data carries no version, so an 'outdated' breakdown isn't available.

sdsc-ordes/tripsu.name: Documentation Discoverability
sdsc-ordes/tripsu.question: Can a newcomer find the docs?
sdsc-ordes/tripsu.description: Scores four discoverability signals from the GME-extracted metadata — a README, a homepage / docs link, a wiki, and a GitHub Pages site.
sdsc-ordes/tripsu.label: documentation signals present
sdsc-ordes/tripsu.secondary: README, Homepage / docs link, Wiki, Pages site
sdsc-ordes/tripsu.unification: Fraction of four boolean signals present (README · homepage · wiki · pages).
sdsc-ordes/tripsu.notes: Four discoverability signals from the GME-extracted metadata: a README file, a homepage / documentation link, a project wiki, and a GitHub Pages site. A high score means a newcomer can find the docs without reading the source.

sdsc-ordes/tripsu.name: License Coverage
sdsc-ordes/tripsu.question: Does the project declare a license?
sdsc-ordes/tripsu.description: Whether the repo declares an SPDX license. Per-repo it's yes/no; the project mean reads as the share of repositories with a declared license.
sdsc-ordes/tripsu.label: declared license
sdsc-ordes/tripsu.unification: 1 if ``license_spdx`` is set, else 0; project mean = coverage.
sdsc-ordes/tripsu.notes: Whether the repository declares a license (SPDX id from the GME ``license_spdx`` field). Per-repo it's yes/no; across a project the mean is the share of repositories that declare a license. Per-*file* coverage needs file-level scanning, which isn't collected — this is the repo-level signal.

sdsc-ordes/tripsu.name: Release Frequency
sdsc-ordes/tripsu.question: How often does it ship releases?
sdsc-ordes/tripsu.description: Lifetime release cadence — releases per year across the span from first to latest release, from the GME `gme-internal:release_count` / `first_release_date` / `latest_release_date` scalars.
sdsc-ordes/tripsu.label: no release data
sdsc-ordes/tripsu.unification: ``gme-internal:release_count`` / ``first_release_date`` / ``latest_release_date`` → releases per year over the span.
sdsc-ordes/tripsu.notes: No ``gme-internal:release_count`` triple for this repo yet. It populates once the repo is extracted with the develop GME (which derives flat release scalars from the GitHub releases list).

sdsc-ordes/tripsu.name: Test Coverage
sdsc-ordes/tripsu.question: Is the test suite measured?
sdsc-ordes/tripsu.description: Static test-coverage percentage advertised in the README, parsed with the GME's deterministic rule (shields.io badge or `coverage: NN%`). Dynamic codecov/coveralls badges carry no number, so they read as no-number, not 0%.
sdsc-ordes/tripsu.label: no coverage number
sdsc-ordes/tripsu.unification: Prefer ``gme-internal:test_coverage`` from the graph; fall back to the GME ``parse_test_coverage`` rule over the README card.
sdsc-ordes/tripsu.notes: No static coverage percentage in the GME graph or the README. Dynamic codecov/coveralls badges carry no number in the markup — those read as no-number (matching the GME's deterministic parser), not 0%.

sdsc-ordes/tripsu.name: Committers
sdsc-ordes/tripsu.question: Who landed code recently?
sdsc-ordes/tripsu.description: Distinct people who committed code in the window (deduplicated committer identities). Narrower than Contributors — counts who landed the commit, not every patch author.
sdsc-ordes/tripsu.label: committers · last 365 days
sdsc-ordes/tripsu.unification: Distinct committer identities (``Commit_uuid``) on windowed commits via an **OpenSearch** cardinality agg.
sdsc-ordes/tripsu.notes: Distinct committer identities (``Commit_uuid``) on commits GrimoireLab indexed in the window. Committers are whoever landed the commit — narrower than *contributors* (``author_name``), which also counts authors whose patch someone else committed.

sdsc-ordes/tripsu.name: Issue Response Time
sdsc-ordes/tripsu.question: How fast do issues get a first reply?
sdsc-ordes/tripsu.description: Median hours from issue creation to the first non-author, non-bot response. Issues only (`pull_request:false`) — the issue-scoped sibling of Time to First Response.
sdsc-ordes/tripsu.label: no answered issues in window
sdsc-ordes/tripsu.unification: P50 of GrimoireLab's `time_to_first_attention_without_bot` on issues (`pull_request:false`) via an **OpenSearch** percentiles agg.
sdsc-ordes/tripsu.notes: No issues in the window carried a time_to_first_attention_without_bot value — either no issues opened, or none answered yet.

sdsc-ordes/wedowind.name: Contributors
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.question: Is there a community at all?
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.description: Distinct people who contributed to the repository. Computed against all three stores so the page exposes both the windowed view (OpenSearch / SPARQL) and the all-time graph view (Neo4j).
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.label: last 365 days · OpenSearch
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.unification: Largest non-zero of three stores: **OpenSearch** (windowed git-cardinality) · **SPARQL** (windowed contribution graph) · **Neo4j** (all-time edges). Fallback ladder skips zeros so an empty index can't hide a real signal.
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.notes: OpenSearch counts distinct ``author_uuid`` values (SortingHat-merged identities, so a person's aliases count once) on commits indexed by GrimoireLab in the window. SPARQL uses the typed ``pulse:lastContributionDate`` on the Contribution node. Neo4j is an all-time edge count — it ignores the window.

sdsc-ordes/wedowind.name: New Contributors
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.question: Is the community growing?
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.description: People whose *first* contribution to this repository falls inside the chosen window. SPARQL uses the typed first-date on the Contribution node; OpenSearch computes the min commit date per author client-side.
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.label: last 365 days · SPARQL
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.notes: A *new* contributor is one whose first contribution to this repo falls inside the window — not necessarily their first ever contribution to anything. Counts can differ between SPARQL and OpenSearch because the crawler deduplicates by GitHub login while GrimoireLab buckets by git author_name (which may include several aliases per person).

sdsc-ordes/wedowind.name: Technical Fork
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.question: How often is the project being reused / developed from?
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.description: Total fork count. The GitHub-reported number comes from SPARQL (latest crawl). Neo4j gives the in-graph count — the subset of those forks the crawler has actually walked.
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.label: forks (GitHub-reported)
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.notes: A snapshot, not a time-series. The GitHub-reported count (SPARQL) is authoritative; the Neo4j count is the subset the crawler has actually enqueued and walked.

sdsc-ordes/wedowind.name: Licenses Declared
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.question: Is the software legally usable and reusable?
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.description: Whether the repository declares one or more licenses (schema:license triple). Doesn't yet check the LICENSE file directly — that's the *License Coverage* metric (Phase 2 / would-like-to-have).
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.label: Apache-2.0
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.notes: Snapshot — the SPARQL store keeps the latest crawl's license triple. Re-enriching this repo will update it. A ✓ here doesn't guarantee the license is OSI-approved (that's a separate CHAOSS metric).

sdsc-ordes/wedowind.name: Academic OS Project Impact
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.question: How much does the software influence academic outputs?
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.description: Proxy via the SPARQL graph: scholarly articles whose authors also have a pulse:hasContribution to this repo. No RAG / vector search — fully reproducible by hand from the /databases console.
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.label: no linked academic articles
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.unification: Count of **SPARQL** shared-author chain results: `Article → schema:author → Person → pulse:hasContribution → Repo` (no direct article↔repo predicate exists yet).
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.notes: The current ontology has no direct article ↔ repo predicate, so this metric uses a shared-author chain: papers whose author also has a pulse:hasContribution to this repo. A zero can mean the contributors haven't linked publications in Infoscience, the publications are crawled but with un-matched author IDs, or simply that there are none. It does NOT mean no paper cites the software.

sdsc-ordes/wedowind.name: Project Popularity
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.question: How visible is the project?
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.description: Composite snapshot: stars + forks from the SPARQL store, and *dependents* from inbound DEPENDS_ON edges in Neo4j — i.e. other repositories that list this one in their package manifest.
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.label: stars
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.notes: Snapshot. Stars and forks come from the latest metadata crawl; the dependents count comes from inbound DEPENDS_ON edges resolved from package manifests (npm, pypi, cargo, go.mod, …) — only as complete as the crawl pipeline that extracted them.

sdsc-ordes/wedowind.name: Programming Language Distribution
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.question: Which languages does the codebase use?
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.description: Distinct schema:programmingLanguage values declared for this repo. Per-language byte shares aren't in the ontology yet, so this is a presence-set.
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.label: no language declared
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.unification: Distinct `schema:programmingLanguage` triples in **SPARQL** (presence, not byte share — that's a Phase-3 ontology upgrade).
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.notes: The metadata extractor didn't surface any language for this repo. Re-running enrichment will refresh the triples.

sdsc-ordes/wedowind.name: Activity Dates and Times
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.question: What is the engagement pattern?
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.description: Monthly commit histogram from GrimoireLab. The card renders it as an inline sparkline so you can see steady vs bursty activity at a glance.
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.label: commits (last 1 year)
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.notes: Date histogram on GrimoireLab's ``grimoire_creation_date`` field. Each bar = one calendar month. Bursty patterns (release-tag spikes) tell a different story from steady monthly contributions.

sdsc-ordes/wedowind.name: Change Request Closure Ratio
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.question: Are pull requests being acted on?
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.description: Closed / total pull requests in the window, with merged vs simply-closed broken out in the secondary line — tells an active-reviewers project from a stalled one.
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.label: closed (last 1 year)
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.secondary: 2 closed of 3 PRs · 2 merged · 1 still open
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.notes: Closure ratio = closed / total. CHAOSS distinguishes *acceptance* (merged) from *closure* (closed without merge); the secondary line shows both so you can tell an active-reviewers project from a graveyard.

sdsc-ordes/wedowind.name: Organizational Diversity
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.question: Is the contributor base single-vendor or distributed?
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.description: Distinct organisations whose members appear in the repo's contributor pool, walked through the Person → Membership → Org chain in SPARQL.
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.label: ownership orgs reachable
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.secondary: Swiss Data Science Center, https://github.com/sdsc-ordes, sdsc-ordes, omnibenchmark
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.unification: Distinct organisations reachable from the repo's contributors via the **Path-1** ownership chain: `Contributor → other repos they touch → pulse:ownedBy → Org`. Ignores self-declared affiliations (Path 2) until upstream name-canonicalisation lands.
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.notes:
Snapshot. Counts distinct ``org:Organization`` entities that own any repository the contributors of *this* repo also work on. CHAOSS reads this as a sustainability signal: a high number = the project's contributor base spans many GitHub organisations.

Uses **Path 1** (ownership) only — the affiliation chain via ``org:hasMembership`` produced noisier counts because self-declared institutional names are not yet canonicalised upstream.

sdsc-ordes/wedowind.name: Time to First Response
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.question: How quickly does the project respond?
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.description: Median hours from PR / issue creation to the first non-bot, non-author comment. Uses GrimoireLab's precomputed ``time_to_first_attention_without_bot``.
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.label: no responses in window
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.unification: P50 of GrimoireLab's pre-computed `time_to_first_attention_without_bot` enrichment via an **OpenSearch** percentiles agg.
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.notes: No github documents in the window carried a time_to_first_attention_without_bot value — either no PRs/issues opened, or none have been responded to yet.

sdsc-ordes/wedowind.name: Issue Resolution Duration
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.question: How long do issues stay open?
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.description: Median days from issue creation to close (PRs excluded). Uses GrimoireLab's ``time_open_days`` enrichment so the answer stays consistent across GitHub backends.
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.label: no closed issues in window
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.unification: P50 of GrimoireLab's `time_open_days` for issues (`pull_request:false`) that closed in the window — via **OpenSearch** percentiles agg.
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.notes: No issues closed in the window for this repo.

sdsc-ordes/wedowind.name: Self Merge Rate
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.question: How strong is the code-review culture?
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.description: Fraction of merged PRs in the window where the author also performed the merge. High = no reviewer gate; low = reviewed by someone else before landing.
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.label: self-merged (last 1 year)
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.notes: CHAOSS treats self-merge rate as a code-review-culture signal: a high number suggests there is no reviewer gate. Some projects intentionally allow it (trusted maintainers, automation merges, single-author repos) so interpret in context.

sdsc-ordes/wedowind.name: Burstiness
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.question: Is contribution steady or in bursts?
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.description: B = (σ − μ) / (σ + μ) on inter-arrival days between commits — Goh & Barabási's burstiness measure. −1 = strictly periodic; 0 = Poisson-like random; +1 = heavy bursts with long silences between them.
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.label: periodic (steady cadence)
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.secondary: 4 active days · mean gap 1.0 d · σ 0.0 d
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.notes: B = (σ − μ) / (σ + μ) on inter-arrival days between commits, per Goh & Barabási (2008). Range: −1 (strictly periodic) through 0 (random Poisson) to +1 (heavy bursts with long silences). Computed client-side from a daily histogram — multiple commits in a single calendar day collapse to one event, so the score is a day-granularity approximation of the per-commit measure CHAOSS defines. The query shown above is exactly what ran.

sdsc-ordes/wedowind.name: Contributor Absence Factor
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.question: Does the project depend on a few people?
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.description: The 'bus factor' — smallest N contributors whose combined commits make up at least 50 % of the project's total. Low values flag a sustainability risk.
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.label: fragile · one or two key people
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.secondary: top 1 of 2 contributors carry 90% of 10 commits
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.notes: Also known as the 'bus factor'. CHAOSS defines it as the smallest N for which the top-N contributors' commits sum to at least half of the project's total. A factor of 1 means a single person could disappear and the project loses half its bandwidth overnight.

sdsc-ordes/wedowind.name: Project Demographics
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.question: Who are the contributors and how active are they?
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.description: Population breakdown of the all-time contributor pool: total / 'core' (top N covering 80 % of commits) / recent arrivals (first commit in last 90 d) / dormant (no commit in 180 d).
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.label: total contributors (all-time, OpenSearch)
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.secondary: core 2 (80 % of 29 commits) · recent arrivals 0 (last 90 d) · dormant 0 (no commit in 180 d)
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.notes: Demographics rolled up from the same git_*_enriched index that powers the activity sparkline. 'Core' uses CHAOSS's 80 % threshold (vs the bus-factor's 50 %); 'recent' marks first-time contributors in the last 90 days; 'dormant' marks people whose last commit on this repo predates the last 180 days.

sdsc-ordes/wedowind.name: Bot Activity
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.question: How much of the activity is automated?
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.description: Share of commits authored by recognised bots (dependabot, renovate, github-actions, *[bot]*, …). High is not bad — it usually means active automation — but it distorts raw commit counts.
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.label: bot share (last 1 year)
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.secondary: 0 of 10 commits matched a bot pattern
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.notes: Primary signal is GrimoireLab's ``author_bot: true`` enrichment flag — set by the SortingHat / Perceval pipeline based on its own heuristics. We also OR-match well-known wildcard patterns ('*[bot]*', '*-bot', 'bot-*', '*github-actions*', '*dependabot*', '*renovate*', '*pre-commit-ci*', '*release-please*', '*stale*', '*mergify*') so a custom CI identity that GrimoireLab hasn't seen is still picked up. A high share is not bad in itself — it usually means Dependabot is active or release-please is signing tags.

sdsc-ordes/wedowind.name: Issues New
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.question: How fast is the backlog growing?
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.description: Issues opened on the repo in the window (excludes PRs). Compare with Issues Closed to see whether inflow is outpacing the team's outflow.
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.label: opened (last 1 year)
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.notes: All issues created on this repo in the window, excluding pull requests. A spike here without a matching spike in issues_closed indicates growing backlog.

sdsc-ordes/wedowind.name: Issues Active
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.question: How alive is the issue tracker?
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.description: Issues with any kind of update (comment, label, state change) inside the window — a liveness signal stronger than just 'were issues opened'.
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.label: touched (last 1 year)
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.notes: Issues that received any update (new comment, label, state change) in the window. Excludes PRs.

sdsc-ordes/wedowind.name: Issues Closed
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.question: How much backlog is the team clearing?
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.description: Issues whose state flipped to closed inside the window.
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.label: closed (last 1 year)
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.notes: Issues whose ``state`` flipped to closed inside the window. Pair with issues_new for an inflow vs outflow view of the backlog.

sdsc-ordes/wedowind.name: Change Request Reviews
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.question: Is work being reviewed before it lands?
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.description: Pull requests that received at least one non-bot review comment in the window. Pair with self_merge to read the code-review culture.
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.label: reviewed PRs (last 1 year)
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.secondary: 2 of 3 PRs (67%) had a non-bot review
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.unification: PRs where **OpenSearch** `github-pull_enriched.num_review_comments > 0` — filter agg inside a windowed PR query.
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.notes: Counts PRs whose ``num_review_comments`` is positive — i.e. at least one review comment from a human. Pair with self_merge to read code-review culture.

sdsc-ordes/wedowind.name: Code Changes Lines
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.question: How much code is being touched?
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.description: Sum of lines added and removed across commits in the window, with the file-change count surfaced as secondary.
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.label: lines changed (last 1 year)
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.secondary: +9,998 added · −3,927 removed · 10 commits · 255 file-changes · ~1,392 lines / commit
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.unification: `sum(lines_added) + sum(lines_removed)` across commits in window from **OpenSearch**. Monthly churn histogram drives the sparkline.
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.notes: Sums GrimoireLab's per-commit ``lines_added`` and ``lines_removed``. Vendored or generated files inflate this — a one-line refactor can still touch thousands of lines if a lockfile lives in the repo.

sdsc-ordes/wedowind.name: Inactive Contributors
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.question: Who has stopped contributing?
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.description: Distinct people who *have* contributed to the repo at some point but whose most recent commit predates the selected window. Pair with `contributors` for the active side of the same ledger.
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.label: no commit in last 1 year
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.unification: Single **OpenSearch** terms agg on ``author_name`` with a ``max(grimoire_creation_date)`` sub-agg. Bucket is inactive if its max-date predates the cutoff (now − 365d), counted client-side.
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.notes: Counts authors who **have** contributed at some point but whose most recent commit is older than the window. Pair with ``contributors`` for the live-side balance. A rising inactive share is a sustainability warning signal.

sdsc-ordes/wedowind.name: Occasional Contributors
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.question: How many drive-by contributors does the project attract?
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.description: Distinct authors with at most 4 commits in the window — the CHAOSS catalogue's drive-by threshold. A community-health signal: high outreach vs low retention.
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.label: ≤ 4 commits in window
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.unification: Terms agg on ``author_name`` filtered to the window, then a client-side count of buckets whose ``doc_count`` is at most 4.
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.notes: Threshold 4 mirrors the CHAOSS catalogue's **Occasional Contributors** definition (drive-by contributors). A high occasional-vs-core ratio means outreach is working but retention isn't.

sdsc-ordes/wedowind.name: Change Request Accepted
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.question: How many PRs shipped?
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.description: Merged pull requests in the window. The acceptance half of `closure_ratio`; pair with `cr_declined` to read the merge-vs-reject split.
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.label: merged prs (last 1 year)
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.unification: Count of **OpenSearch** ``github-pull_enriched`` docs with ``pull_request:true`` + ``merged:true`` + ``merged_at`` in the window.
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.notes: The acceptance half of ``closure_ratio`` — PRs that actually shipped. Pair with ``cr_declined`` to read the accept/reject split.

sdsc-ordes/wedowind.name: Change Request Declined
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.question: How many PRs were rejected?
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.description: Pull requests closed without merging — explicit rejections or stale work cleaned up by maintainers.
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.label: declined prs (last 1 year)
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.unification: Count of **OpenSearch** ``github-pull_enriched`` docs with ``pull_request:true`` + ``state:closed`` + ``merged:false`` + ``closed_at`` in window.
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.notes: Closed-without-merge PRs — explicit rejections or stale work the maintainers closed without shipping. The other half of ``cr_accepted``.

sdsc-ordes/wedowind.name: Change Request Duration
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.question: How fast do PRs that ship actually ship?
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.description: Median days from PR creation to merge for PRs that merged in the window. Acceptance-speed view.
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.label: median days from pr open to merge (last 1 year)
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.unification: P50 of GrimoireLab's ``time_open_days`` on ``github-pull_enriched`` PRs where ``merged:true`` and ``merged_at`` falls inside the window.
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.notes: Acceptance speed — the time from PR open to merge for PRs that actually shipped. A rising number can signal a review-capacity squeeze.

sdsc-ordes/wedowind.name: Time to Close (PRs)
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.question: How long do PRs stay open?
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.description: Median days from PR creation to close — counts ALL closed PRs (merged + declined). Differs from `cr_duration` which is merge-only.
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.label: median days from pr open to close (last 1 year)
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.unification: P50 of GrimoireLab's ``time_open_days`` on ``github-pull_enriched`` PRs where ``state:closed`` (merged or declined) and ``closed_at`` is in the window.
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.notes: Time-to-close considers *all* closed PRs — merged + declined. Differs from ``cr_duration`` which is acceptance-speed only. A wide gap between the two means the project closes-without-merging slowly.

sdsc-ordes/wedowind.name: Upstream Code Dependencies
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.question: What does this project build on?
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.description: Count of distinct upstream repositories this project depends on, resolved from its dependency manifests into the Neo4j `DEPENDS_ON` graph.
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.label: direct upstream dependencies
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.unification: Single Cypher ``count(DISTINCT dep)`` over outbound ``DEPENDS_ON`` edges from the repo node.
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.notes: Counts distinct outbound ``DEPENDS_ON`` edges resolved to concrete upstream repositories. Reflects what the crawler resolved from dependency manifests — unresolved / private packages aren't edges, so this is a floor, not the full lock-file count. Edge data carries no version, so an 'outdated' breakdown isn't available.

sdsc-ordes/wedowind.name: Documentation Discoverability
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.question: Can a newcomer find the docs?
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.description: Scores four discoverability signals from the GME-extracted metadata — a README, a homepage / docs link, a wiki, and a GitHub Pages site.
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.label: documentation signals present
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.unification: Fraction of four boolean signals present (README · homepage · wiki · pages).
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.notes: Four discoverability signals from the GME-extracted metadata: a README file, a homepage / documentation link, a project wiki, and a GitHub Pages site. A high score means a newcomer can find the docs without reading the source.

sdsc-ordes/wedowind.name: License Coverage
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.question: Does the project declare a license?
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.description: Whether the repo declares an SPDX license. Per-repo it's yes/no; the project mean reads as the share of repositories with a declared license.
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.label: declared license
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.unification: 1 if ``license_spdx`` is set, else 0; project mean = coverage.
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.notes: Whether the repository declares a license (SPDX id from the GME ``license_spdx`` field). Per-repo it's yes/no; across a project the mean is the share of repositories that declare a license. Per-*file* coverage needs file-level scanning, which isn't collected — this is the repo-level signal.

sdsc-ordes/wedowind.name: Release Frequency
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.question: How often does it ship releases?
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.description: Lifetime release cadence — releases per year across the span from first to latest release, from the GME `gme-internal:release_count` / `first_release_date` / `latest_release_date` scalars.
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.label: no release data
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.unification: ``gme-internal:release_count`` / ``first_release_date`` / ``latest_release_date`` → releases per year over the span.
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.notes: No ``gme-internal:release_count`` triple for this repo yet. It populates once the repo is extracted with the develop GME (which derives flat release scalars from the GitHub releases list).

sdsc-ordes/wedowind.name: Test Coverage
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.question: Is the test suite measured?
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.description: Static test-coverage percentage advertised in the README, parsed with the GME's deterministic rule (shields.io badge or `coverage: NN%`). Dynamic codecov/coveralls badges carry no number, so they read as no-number, not 0%.
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.label: no coverage number
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.unification: Prefer ``gme-internal:test_coverage`` from the graph; fall back to the GME ``parse_test_coverage`` rule over the README card.
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.notes: No static coverage percentage in the GME graph or the README. Dynamic codecov/coveralls badges carry no number in the markup — those read as no-number (matching the GME's deterministic parser), not 0%.

sdsc-ordes/wedowind.name: Committers
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.question: Who landed code recently?
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.description: Distinct people who committed code in the window (deduplicated committer identities). Narrower than Contributors — counts who landed the commit, not every patch author.
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.label: committers · last 365 days
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.unification: Distinct committer identities (``Commit_uuid``) on windowed commits via an **OpenSearch** cardinality agg.
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.notes: Distinct committer identities (``Commit_uuid``) on commits GrimoireLab indexed in the window. Committers are whoever landed the commit — narrower than *contributors* (``author_name``), which also counts authors whose patch someone else committed.

sdsc-ordes/wedowind.name: Issue Response Time
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.question: How fast do issues get a first reply?
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.description: Median hours from issue creation to the first non-author, non-bot response. Issues only (`pull_request:false`) — the issue-scoped sibling of Time to First Response.
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.label: no answered issues in window
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.unification: P50 of GrimoireLab's `time_to_first_attention_without_bot` on issues (`pull_request:false`) via an **OpenSearch** percentiles agg.
sdsc-ordes/wedowind.notes: No issues in the window carried a time_to_first_attention_without_bot value — either no issues opened, or none answered yet.

sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.name: Contributors
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.question: Is there a community at all?
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.description: Distinct people who contributed to the repository. Computed against all three stores so the page exposes both the windowed view (OpenSearch / SPARQL) and the all-time graph view (Neo4j).
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.label: all-time · Neo4j community graph
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.unification: Largest non-zero of three stores: **OpenSearch** (windowed git-cardinality) · **SPARQL** (windowed contribution graph) · **Neo4j** (all-time edges). Fallback ladder skips zeros so an empty index can't hide a real signal.
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.notes: OpenSearch counts distinct ``author_uuid`` values (SortingHat-merged identities, so a person's aliases count once) on commits indexed by GrimoireLab in the window. SPARQL uses the typed ``pulse:lastContributionDate`` on the Contribution node. Neo4j is an all-time edge count — it ignores the window.

sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.name: New Contributors
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.question: Is the community growing?
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.description: People whose *first* contribution to this repository falls inside the chosen window. SPARQL uses the typed first-date on the Contribution node; OpenSearch computes the min commit date per author client-side.
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.label: last 365 days · SPARQL
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.notes: A *new* contributor is one whose first contribution to this repo falls inside the window — not necessarily their first ever contribution to anything. Counts can differ between SPARQL and OpenSearch because the crawler deduplicates by GitHub login while GrimoireLab buckets by git author_name (which may include several aliases per person).

sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.name: Technical Fork
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.question: How often is the project being reused / developed from?
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.description: Total fork count. The GitHub-reported number comes from SPARQL (latest crawl). Neo4j gives the in-graph count — the subset of those forks the crawler has actually walked.
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.label: forks (GitHub-reported)
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.notes: A snapshot, not a time-series. The GitHub-reported count (SPARQL) is authoritative; the Neo4j count is the subset the crawler has actually enqueued and walked.

sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.name: Licenses Declared
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.question: Is the software legally usable and reusable?
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.description: Whether the repository declares one or more licenses (schema:license triple). Doesn't yet check the LICENSE file directly — that's the *License Coverage* metric (Phase 2 / would-like-to-have).
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.label: MIT
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.notes: Snapshot — the SPARQL store keeps the latest crawl's license triple. Re-enriching this repo will update it. A ✓ here doesn't guarantee the license is OSI-approved (that's a separate CHAOSS metric).

sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.name: Academic OS Project Impact
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.question: How much does the software influence academic outputs?
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.description: Proxy via the SPARQL graph: scholarly articles whose authors also have a pulse:hasContribution to this repo. No RAG / vector search — fully reproducible by hand from the /databases console.
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.label: no linked academic articles
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.unification: Count of **SPARQL** shared-author chain results: `Article → schema:author → Person → pulse:hasContribution → Repo` (no direct article↔repo predicate exists yet).
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.notes: The current ontology has no direct article ↔ repo predicate, so this metric uses a shared-author chain: papers whose author also has a pulse:hasContribution to this repo. A zero can mean the contributors haven't linked publications in Infoscience, the publications are crawled but with un-matched author IDs, or simply that there are none. It does NOT mean no paper cites the software.

sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.name: Project Popularity
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.question: How visible is the project?
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.description: Composite snapshot: stars + forks from the SPARQL store, and *dependents* from inbound DEPENDS_ON edges in Neo4j — i.e. other repositories that list this one in their package manifest.
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.label: stars
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.notes: Snapshot. Stars and forks come from the latest metadata crawl; the dependents count comes from inbound DEPENDS_ON edges resolved from package manifests (npm, pypi, cargo, go.mod, …) — only as complete as the crawl pipeline that extracted them.

sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.name: Programming Language Distribution
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.question: Which languages does the codebase use?
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.description: Distinct schema:programmingLanguage values declared for this repo. Per-language byte shares aren't in the ontology yet, so this is a presence-set.
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.label: languages
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.notes: Snapshot. The current ontology stores languages as a flat set — no per-language size weighting. The CHAOSS 'Programming Language Distribution' spec wants byte-level shares; that's Phase 3 once the extractor emits them.

sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.name: Activity Dates and Times
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.question: What is the engagement pattern?
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.description: Monthly commit histogram from GrimoireLab. The card renders it as an inline sparkline so you can see steady vs bursty activity at a glance.
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.label: no commits in window
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.unification: Sum of monthly bucket counts from one **OpenSearch** `date_histogram` on `grimoire_creation_date`.
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.notes: Either this repo isn't indexed by GrimoireLab or it had no commits in the selected window. The /hub entity page's sparkline runs the same agg over all time.

sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.name: Change Request Closure Ratio
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.question: Are pull requests being acted on?
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.description: Closed / total pull requests in the window, with merged vs simply-closed broken out in the secondary line — tells an active-reviewers project from a stalled one.
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.label: no PRs in window
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.unification: `closed / total` from one **OpenSearch** PR aggregation (`state.terms` + `merged` filter on PRs created in window).
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.notes: Either no pull requests were opened in this window, or GrimoireLab hasn't ingested this repo's github stream yet.

sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.name: Organizational Diversity
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.question: Is the contributor base single-vendor or distributed?
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.description: Distinct organisations whose members appear in the repo's contributor pool, walked through the Person → Membership → Org chain in SPARQL.
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.label: ownership orgs reachable
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.secondary: Swiss Data Science Center, https://github.com/sdsc-ordes, sdsc-ordes, biocypher, omnibenchmark
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.unification: Distinct organisations reachable from the repo's contributors via the **Path-1** ownership chain: `Contributor → other repos they touch → pulse:ownedBy → Org`. Ignores self-declared affiliations (Path 2) until upstream name-canonicalisation lands.
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.notes:
Snapshot. Counts distinct ``org:Organization`` entities that own any repository the contributors of *this* repo also work on. CHAOSS reads this as a sustainability signal: a high number = the project's contributor base spans many GitHub organisations.

Uses **Path 1** (ownership) only — the affiliation chain via ``org:hasMembership`` produced noisier counts because self-declared institutional names are not yet canonicalised upstream.

sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.name: Time to First Response
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.question: How quickly does the project respond?
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.description: Median hours from PR / issue creation to the first non-bot, non-author comment. Uses GrimoireLab's precomputed ``time_to_first_attention_without_bot``.
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.label: no responses in window
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.unification: P50 of GrimoireLab's pre-computed `time_to_first_attention_without_bot` enrichment via an **OpenSearch** percentiles agg.
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.notes: No github documents in the window carried a time_to_first_attention_without_bot value — either no PRs/issues opened, or none have been responded to yet.

sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.name: Issue Resolution Duration
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.question: How long do issues stay open?
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.description: Median days from issue creation to close (PRs excluded). Uses GrimoireLab's ``time_open_days`` enrichment so the answer stays consistent across GitHub backends.
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.label: no closed issues in window
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.unification: P50 of GrimoireLab's `time_open_days` for issues (`pull_request:false`) that closed in the window — via **OpenSearch** percentiles agg.
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.notes: No issues closed in the window for this repo.

sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.name: Self Merge Rate
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.question: How strong is the code-review culture?
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.description: Fraction of merged PRs in the window where the author also performed the merge. High = no reviewer gate; low = reviewed by someone else before landing.
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.label: no merged PRs in window
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.unification: `self-merged / total-merged` — Painless script compares `user_login` vs `merge_author_login` inside an **OpenSearch** filter agg.
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.notes: No PRs merged on this repo in the window.

sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.name: Burstiness
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.question: Is contribution steady or in bursts?
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.description: B = (σ − μ) / (σ + μ) on inter-arrival days between commits — Goh & Barabási's burstiness measure. −1 = strictly periodic; 0 = Poisson-like random; +1 = heavy bursts with long silences between them.
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.label: only 0 active days
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.unification: B = (σ − μ) / (σ + μ) on inter-arrival days between commit-days. Daily histogram from **OpenSearch**, post-processed in Python (`statistics.pstdev` + mean).
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.notes: Burstiness needs at least three active days in the window to compute inter-arrival gaps. Widen the window or pick a more active repo.

sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.name: Contributor Absence Factor
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.question: Does the project depend on a few people?
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.description: The 'bus factor' — smallest N contributors whose combined commits make up at least 50 % of the project's total. Low values flag a sustainability risk.
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.label: no commits in window
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.unification: Walk descending **OpenSearch** terms agg until cumulative commits ≥ 50 %. Headline = N at threshold; example list shows each top contributor's share.
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.notes: Widen the window — the bus factor needs at least one commit.

sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.name: Project Demographics
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.question: Who are the contributors and how active are they?
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.description: Population breakdown of the all-time contributor pool: total / 'core' (top N covering 80 % of commits) / recent arrivals (first commit in last 90 d) / dormant (no commit in 180 d).
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.label: total contributors (all-time, OpenSearch)
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.secondary: core 2 (80 % of 46 commits) · recent arrivals 0 (last 90 d) · dormant 2 (no commit in 180 d)
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.notes: Demographics rolled up from the same git_*_enriched index that powers the activity sparkline. 'Core' uses CHAOSS's 80 % threshold (vs the bus-factor's 50 %); 'recent' marks first-time contributors in the last 90 days; 'dormant' marks people whose last commit on this repo predates the last 180 days.

sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.name: Bot Activity
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.question: How much of the activity is automated?
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.description: Share of commits authored by recognised bots (dependabot, renovate, github-actions, *[bot]*, …). High is not bad — it usually means active automation — but it distorts raw commit counts.
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.label: no commits in window
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.unification: bot-matching commits / total. Detection = **OpenSearch** `author_bot:true` OR any of 10 wildcard author-name patterns (`*[bot]*`, `*dependabot*`, …).
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.notes: Widen the window to compute bot share.

sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.name: Issues New
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.question: How fast is the backlog growing?
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.description: Issues opened on the repo in the window (excludes PRs). Compare with Issues Closed to see whether inflow is outpacing the team's outflow.
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.label: opened (last 1 year)
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.notes: All issues created on this repo in the window, excluding pull requests. A spike here without a matching spike in issues_closed indicates growing backlog.

sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.name: Issues Active
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.question: How alive is the issue tracker?
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.description: Issues with any kind of update (comment, label, state change) inside the window — a liveness signal stronger than just 'were issues opened'.
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.label: touched (last 1 year)
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.notes: Issues that received any update (new comment, label, state change) in the window. Excludes PRs.

sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.name: Issues Closed
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.question: How much backlog is the team clearing?
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.description: Issues whose state flipped to closed inside the window.
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.label: closed (last 1 year)
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.notes: Issues whose ``state`` flipped to closed inside the window. Pair with issues_new for an inflow vs outflow view of the backlog.

sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.name: Change Request Reviews
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.question: Is work being reviewed before it lands?
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.description: Pull requests that received at least one non-bot review comment in the window. Pair with self_merge to read the code-review culture.
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.label: no PRs in window
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.unification: PRs where **OpenSearch** `github-pull_enriched.num_review_comments > 0` — filter agg inside a windowed PR query.
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.notes: No pull requests opened on this repo in the window.

sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.name: Code Changes Lines
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.question: How much code is being touched?
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.description: Sum of lines added and removed across commits in the window, with the file-change count surfaced as secondary.
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.label: no commits in window
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.unification: `sum(lines_added) + sum(lines_removed)` across commits in window from **OpenSearch**. Monthly churn histogram drives the sparkline.
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.notes: Widen the window to compute line churn.

sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.name: Inactive Contributors
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.question: Who has stopped contributing?
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.description: Distinct people who *have* contributed to the repo at some point but whose most recent commit predates the selected window. Pair with `contributors` for the active side of the same ledger.
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.label: no commit in last 1 year
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.unification: Single **OpenSearch** terms agg on ``author_name`` with a ``max(grimoire_creation_date)`` sub-agg. Bucket is inactive if its max-date predates the cutoff (now − 365d), counted client-side.
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.notes: Counts authors who **have** contributed at some point but whose most recent commit is older than the window. Pair with ``contributors`` for the live-side balance. A rising inactive share is a sustainability warning signal.

sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.name: Occasional Contributors
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.question: How many drive-by contributors does the project attract?
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.description: Distinct authors with at most 4 commits in the window — the CHAOSS catalogue's drive-by threshold. A community-health signal: high outreach vs low retention.
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.label: ≤ 4 commits in window
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.unification: Terms agg on ``author_name`` filtered to the window, then a client-side count of buckets whose ``doc_count`` is at most 4.
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.notes: Threshold 4 mirrors the CHAOSS catalogue's **Occasional Contributors** definition (drive-by contributors). A high occasional-vs-core ratio means outreach is working but retention isn't.

sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.name: Change Request Accepted
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.question: How many PRs shipped?
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.description: Merged pull requests in the window. The acceptance half of `closure_ratio`; pair with `cr_declined` to read the merge-vs-reject split.
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.label: merged prs (last 1 year)
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.unification: Count of **OpenSearch** ``github-pull_enriched`` docs with ``pull_request:true`` + ``merged:true`` + ``merged_at`` in the window.
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.notes: The acceptance half of ``closure_ratio`` — PRs that actually shipped. Pair with ``cr_declined`` to read the accept/reject split.

sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.name: Change Request Declined
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.question: How many PRs were rejected?
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.description: Pull requests closed without merging — explicit rejections or stale work cleaned up by maintainers.
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.label: declined prs (last 1 year)
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.unification: Count of **OpenSearch** ``github-pull_enriched`` docs with ``pull_request:true`` + ``state:closed`` + ``merged:false`` + ``closed_at`` in window.
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.notes: Closed-without-merge PRs — explicit rejections or stale work the maintainers closed without shipping. The other half of ``cr_accepted``.

sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.name: Change Request Duration
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.question: How fast do PRs that ship actually ship?
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.description: Median days from PR creation to merge for PRs that merged in the window. Acceptance-speed view.
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.label: no PRs in window
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.unification: P50 of GrimoireLab's ``time_open_days`` on ``github-pull_enriched`` PRs where ``merged:true`` and ``merged_at`` falls inside the window.
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.notes: Acceptance speed — the time from PR open to merge for PRs that actually shipped. A rising number can signal a review-capacity squeeze.

sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.name: Time to Close (PRs)
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.question: How long do PRs stay open?
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.description: Median days from PR creation to close — counts ALL closed PRs (merged + declined). Differs from `cr_duration` which is merge-only.
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.label: no PRs in window
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.unification: P50 of GrimoireLab's ``time_open_days`` on ``github-pull_enriched`` PRs where ``state:closed`` (merged or declined) and ``closed_at`` is in the window.
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.notes: Time-to-close considers *all* closed PRs — merged + declined. Differs from ``cr_duration`` which is acceptance-speed only. A wide gap between the two means the project closes-without-merging slowly.

sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.name: Upstream Code Dependencies
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.question: What does this project build on?
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.description: Count of distinct upstream repositories this project depends on, resolved from its dependency manifests into the Neo4j `DEPENDS_ON` graph.
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.label: direct upstream dependencies
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.unification: Single Cypher ``count(DISTINCT dep)`` over outbound ``DEPENDS_ON`` edges from the repo node.
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.notes: Counts distinct outbound ``DEPENDS_ON`` edges resolved to concrete upstream repositories. Reflects what the crawler resolved from dependency manifests — unresolved / private packages aren't edges, so this is a floor, not the full lock-file count. Edge data carries no version, so an 'outdated' breakdown isn't available.

sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.name: Documentation Discoverability
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.question: Can a newcomer find the docs?
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.description: Scores four discoverability signals from the GME-extracted metadata — a README, a homepage / docs link, a wiki, and a GitHub Pages site.
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.label: documentation signals present
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.secondary: README, Homepage / docs link, Wiki, Pages site
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.unification: Fraction of four boolean signals present (README · homepage · wiki · pages).
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.notes: Four discoverability signals from the GME-extracted metadata: a README file, a homepage / documentation link, a project wiki, and a GitHub Pages site. A high score means a newcomer can find the docs without reading the source.

sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.name: License Coverage
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.question: Does the project declare a license?
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.description: Whether the repo declares an SPDX license. Per-repo it's yes/no; the project mean reads as the share of repositories with a declared license.
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.label: declared license
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.unification: 1 if ``license_spdx`` is set, else 0; project mean = coverage.
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.notes: Whether the repository declares a license (SPDX id from the GME ``license_spdx`` field). Per-repo it's yes/no; across a project the mean is the share of repositories that declare a license. Per-*file* coverage needs file-level scanning, which isn't collected — this is the repo-level signal.

sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.name: Release Frequency
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.question: How often does it ship releases?
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.description: Lifetime release cadence — releases per year across the span from first to latest release, from the GME `gme-internal:release_count` / `first_release_date` / `latest_release_date` scalars.
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.label: no release data
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.unification: ``gme-internal:release_count`` / ``first_release_date`` / ``latest_release_date`` → releases per year over the span.
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.notes: No ``gme-internal:release_count`` triple for this repo yet. It populates once the repo is extracted with the develop GME (which derives flat release scalars from the GitHub releases list).

sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.name: Test Coverage
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.question: Is the test suite measured?
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.description: Static test-coverage percentage advertised in the README, parsed with the GME's deterministic rule (shields.io badge or `coverage: NN%`). Dynamic codecov/coveralls badges carry no number, so they read as no-number, not 0%.
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.label: no coverage number

sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.name: Committers
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.question: Who landed code recently?
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.description: Distinct people who committed code in the window (deduplicated committer identities). Narrower than Contributors — counts who landed the commit, not every patch author.
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.label: committers · last 365 days
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.unification: Distinct committer identities (``Commit_uuid``) on windowed commits via an **OpenSearch** cardinality agg.
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.notes: Distinct committer identities (``Commit_uuid``) on commits GrimoireLab indexed in the window. Committers are whoever landed the commit — narrower than *contributors* (``author_name``), which also counts authors whose patch someone else committed.

sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.name: Issue Response Time
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.question: How fast do issues get a first reply?
sdsc-ordes/workflow-explorer.description: Median hours from issue creation to the first non-author, non-bot response. Issues only (`pull_request:false`) — the issue-scoped sibling of Time to First Response.

sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.name: Contributors
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.question: Is there a community at all?
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.description: Distinct people who contributed to the repository. Computed against all three stores so the page exposes both the windowed view (OpenSearch / SPARQL) and the all-time graph view (Neo4j).
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.label: all-time · Neo4j community graph
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.unification: Largest non-zero of three stores: **OpenSearch** (windowed git-cardinality) · **SPARQL** (windowed contribution graph) · **Neo4j** (all-time edges). Fallback ladder skips zeros so an empty index can't hide a real signal.
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.notes: OpenSearch counts distinct ``author_uuid`` values (SortingHat-merged identities, so a person's aliases count once) on commits indexed by GrimoireLab in the window. SPARQL uses the typed ``pulse:lastContributionDate`` on the Contribution node. Neo4j is an all-time edge count — it ignores the window.

sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.name: New Contributors
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.question: Is the community growing?
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.description: People whose *first* contribution to this repository falls inside the chosen window. SPARQL uses the typed first-date on the Contribution node; OpenSearch computes the min commit date per author client-side.
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.label: last 365 days · SPARQL
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.notes: A *new* contributor is one whose first contribution to this repo falls inside the window — not necessarily their first ever contribution to anything. Counts can differ between SPARQL and OpenSearch because the crawler deduplicates by GitHub login while GrimoireLab buckets by git author_name (which may include several aliases per person).

sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.name: Technical Fork
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.question: How often is the project being reused / developed from?
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.description: Total fork count. The GitHub-reported number comes from SPARQL (latest crawl). Neo4j gives the in-graph count — the subset of those forks the crawler has actually walked.
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.label: forks (GitHub-reported)
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.notes: A snapshot, not a time-series. The GitHub-reported count (SPARQL) is authoritative; the Neo4j count is the subset the crawler has actually enqueued and walked.

sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.name: Licenses Declared
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.question: Is the software legally usable and reusable?
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.description: Whether the repository declares one or more licenses (schema:license triple). Doesn't yet check the LICENSE file directly — that's the *License Coverage* metric (Phase 2 / would-like-to-have).
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.label: MIT
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.notes: Snapshot — the SPARQL store keeps the latest crawl's license triple. Re-enriching this repo will update it. A ✓ here doesn't guarantee the license is OSI-approved (that's a separate CHAOSS metric).

sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.name: Academic OS Project Impact
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.question: How much does the software influence academic outputs?
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.description: Proxy via the SPARQL graph: scholarly articles whose authors also have a pulse:hasContribution to this repo. No RAG / vector search — fully reproducible by hand from the /databases console.
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.label: no linked academic articles
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.unification: Count of **SPARQL** shared-author chain results: `Article → schema:author → Person → pulse:hasContribution → Repo` (no direct article↔repo predicate exists yet).
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.notes: The current ontology has no direct article ↔ repo predicate, so this metric uses a shared-author chain: papers whose author also has a pulse:hasContribution to this repo. A zero can mean the contributors haven't linked publications in Infoscience, the publications are crawled but with un-matched author IDs, or simply that there are none. It does NOT mean no paper cites the software.

sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.name: Project Popularity
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.question: How visible is the project?
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.description: Composite snapshot: stars + forks from the SPARQL store, and *dependents* from inbound DEPENDS_ON edges in Neo4j — i.e. other repositories that list this one in their package manifest.
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.label: stars
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.notes: Snapshot. Stars and forks come from the latest metadata crawl; the dependents count comes from inbound DEPENDS_ON edges resolved from package manifests (npm, pypi, cargo, go.mod, …) — only as complete as the crawl pipeline that extracted them.

sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.name: Programming Language Distribution
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.question: Which languages does the codebase use?
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.description: Distinct schema:programmingLanguage values declared for this repo. Per-language byte shares aren't in the ontology yet, so this is a presence-set.
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.label: languages
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.notes: Snapshot. The current ontology stores languages as a flat set — no per-language size weighting. The CHAOSS 'Programming Language Distribution' spec wants byte-level shares; that's Phase 3 once the extractor emits them.

sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.name: Activity Dates and Times
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.question: What is the engagement pattern?
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.description: Monthly commit histogram from GrimoireLab. The card renders it as an inline sparkline so you can see steady vs bursty activity at a glance.

sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.notes: Either this repo isn't indexed by GrimoireLab or it had no commits in the selected window. The /hub entity page's sparkline runs the same agg over all time.

sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.name: Change Request Closure Ratio
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.question: Are pull requests being acted on?
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.description: Closed / total pull requests in the window, with merged vs simply-closed broken out in the secondary line — tells an active-reviewers project from a stalled one.
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.label: no PRs in window
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.unification: `closed / total` from one **OpenSearch** PR aggregation (`state.terms` + `merged` filter on PRs created in window).
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.notes: Either no pull requests were opened in this window, or GrimoireLab hasn't ingested this repo's github stream yet.

sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.name: Organizational Diversity
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.question: Is the contributor base single-vendor or distributed?
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.description: Distinct organisations whose members appear in the repo's contributor pool, walked through the Person → Membership → Org chain in SPARQL.
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.label: ownership orgs reachable
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.secondary: Swiss Data Science Center, https://github.com/sdsc-ordes, sdsc-ordes
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.unification: Distinct organisations reachable from the repo's contributors via the **Path-1** ownership chain: `Contributor → other repos they touch → pulse:ownedBy → Org`. Ignores self-declared affiliations (Path 2) until upstream name-canonicalisation lands.
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.notes:
Snapshot. Counts distinct ``org:Organization`` entities that own any repository the contributors of *this* repo also work on. CHAOSS reads this as a sustainability signal: a high number = the project's contributor base spans many GitHub organisations.

Uses **Path 1** (ownership) only — the affiliation chain via ``org:hasMembership`` produced noisier counts because self-declared institutional names are not yet canonicalised upstream.

sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.notes: No PRs merged on this repo in the window.

sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.name: Burstiness
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.question: Is contribution steady or in bursts?
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.description: B = (σ − μ) / (σ + μ) on inter-arrival days between commits — Goh & Barabási's burstiness measure. −1 = strictly periodic; 0 = Poisson-like random; +1 = heavy bursts with long silences between them.
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.label: only 0 active days
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.unification: B = (σ − μ) / (σ + μ) on inter-arrival days between commit-days. Daily histogram from **OpenSearch**, post-processed in Python (`statistics.pstdev` + mean).
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.notes: Burstiness needs at least three active days in the window to compute inter-arrival gaps. Widen the window or pick a more active repo.

sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.name: Contributor Absence Factor
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.question: Does the project depend on a few people?
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.description: The 'bus factor' — smallest N contributors whose combined commits make up at least 50 % of the project's total. Low values flag a sustainability risk.
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.label: no commits in window
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.unification: Walk descending **OpenSearch** terms agg until cumulative commits ≥ 50 %. Headline = N at threshold; example list shows each top contributor's share.
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.notes: Widen the window — the bus factor needs at least one commit.

sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.name: Project Demographics
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.question: Who are the contributors and how active are they?

sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.secondary: core 1 (80 % of 54 commits) · recent arrivals 0 (last 90 d) · dormant 3 (no commit in 180 d)
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.notes: Demographics rolled up from the same git_*_enriched index that powers the activity sparkline. 'Core' uses CHAOSS's 80 % threshold (vs the bus-factor's 50 %); 'recent' marks first-time contributors in the last 90 days; 'dormant' marks people whose last commit on this repo predates the last 180 days.

sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.name: Bot Activity
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.question: How much of the activity is automated?
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.description: Share of commits authored by recognised bots (dependabot, renovate, github-actions, *[bot]*, …). High is not bad — it usually means active automation — but it distorts raw commit counts.
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.label: no commits in window
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.unification: bot-matching commits / total. Detection = **OpenSearch** `author_bot:true` OR any of 10 wildcard author-name patterns (`*[bot]*`, `*dependabot*`, …).
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.notes: Widen the window to compute bot share.

sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.name: Issues New
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.question: How fast is the backlog growing?
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.description: Issues opened on the repo in the window (excludes PRs). Compare with Issues Closed to see whether inflow is outpacing the team's outflow.
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.label: opened (last 1 year)
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.notes: All issues created on this repo in the window, excluding pull requests. A spike here without a matching spike in issues_closed indicates growing backlog.

sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.name: Issues Active
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.question: How alive is the issue tracker?
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.description: Issues with any kind of update (comment, label, state change) inside the window — a liveness signal stronger than just 'were issues opened'.
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.label: touched (last 1 year)
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.notes: Issues that received any update (new comment, label, state change) in the window. Excludes PRs.

sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.name: Issues Closed
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.question: How much backlog is the team clearing?
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.description: Issues whose state flipped to closed inside the window.
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.label: closed (last 1 year)
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.notes: Issues whose ``state`` flipped to closed inside the window. Pair with issues_new for an inflow vs outflow view of the backlog.

sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.name: Change Request Reviews
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.question: Is work being reviewed before it lands?
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.description: Pull requests that received at least one non-bot review comment in the window. Pair with self_merge to read the code-review culture.

sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.notes: No pull requests opened on this repo in the window.

sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.name: Code Changes Lines
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.question: How much code is being touched?
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.description: Sum of lines added and removed across commits in the window, with the file-change count surfaced as secondary.
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.label: no commits in window
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.unification: `sum(lines_added) + sum(lines_removed)` across commits in window from **OpenSearch**. Monthly churn histogram drives the sparkline.
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.notes: Widen the window to compute line churn.

sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.name: Inactive Contributors
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.question: Who has stopped contributing?
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.description: Distinct people who *have* contributed to the repo at some point but whose most recent commit predates the selected window. Pair with `contributors` for the active side of the same ledger.
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.label: no commit in last 1 year
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.unification: Single **OpenSearch** terms agg on ``author_name`` with a ``max(grimoire_creation_date)`` sub-agg. Bucket is inactive if its max-date predates the cutoff (now − 365d), counted client-side.
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.notes: Counts authors who **have** contributed at some point but whose most recent commit is older than the window. Pair with ``contributors`` for the live-side balance. A rising inactive share is a sustainability warning signal.

sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.name: Occasional Contributors
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.question: How many drive-by contributors does the project attract?
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.description: Distinct authors with at most 4 commits in the window — the CHAOSS catalogue's drive-by threshold. A community-health signal: high outreach vs low retention.
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.label: ≤ 4 commits in window
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.unification: Terms agg on ``author_name`` filtered to the window, then a client-side count of buckets whose ``doc_count`` is at most 4.
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.notes: Threshold 4 mirrors the CHAOSS catalogue's **Occasional Contributors** definition (drive-by contributors). A high occasional-vs-core ratio means outreach is working but retention isn't.

sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.name: Change Request Accepted
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.question: How many PRs shipped?

sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.notes: The acceptance half of ``closure_ratio`` — PRs that actually shipped. Pair with ``cr_declined`` to read the accept/reject split.

sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.name: Change Request Declined
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.question: How many PRs were rejected?

sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.unification: Count of **OpenSearch** ``github-pull_enriched`` docs with ``pull_request:true`` + ``state:closed`` + ``merged:false`` + ``closed_at`` in window.
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.notes: Closed-without-merge PRs — explicit rejections or stale work the maintainers closed without shipping. The other half of ``cr_accepted``.

sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.name: Change Request Duration
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.question: How fast do PRs that ship actually ship?
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.description: Median days from PR creation to merge for PRs that merged in the window. Acceptance-speed view.
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.label: no PRs in window
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.unification: P50 of GrimoireLab's ``time_open_days`` on ``github-pull_enriched`` PRs where ``merged:true`` and ``merged_at`` falls inside the window.
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.notes: Acceptance speed — the time from PR open to merge for PRs that actually shipped. A rising number can signal a review-capacity squeeze.

sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.name: Time to Close (PRs)
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.question: How long do PRs stay open?
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.description: Median days from PR creation to close — counts ALL closed PRs (merged + declined). Differs from `cr_duration` which is merge-only.
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.label: no PRs in window
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.unification: P50 of GrimoireLab's ``time_open_days`` on ``github-pull_enriched`` PRs where ``state:closed`` (merged or declined) and ``closed_at`` is in the window.
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.notes: Time-to-close considers *all* closed PRs — merged + declined. Differs from ``cr_duration`` which is acceptance-speed only. A wide gap between the two means the project closes-without-merging slowly.

sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.name: Upstream Code Dependencies
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.question: What does this project build on?
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.description: Count of distinct upstream repositories this project depends on, resolved from its dependency manifests into the Neo4j `DEPENDS_ON` graph.
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.label: direct upstream dependencies
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.unification: Single Cypher ``count(DISTINCT dep)`` over outbound ``DEPENDS_ON`` edges from the repo node.
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.notes: Counts distinct outbound ``DEPENDS_ON`` edges resolved to concrete upstream repositories. Reflects what the crawler resolved from dependency manifests — unresolved / private packages aren't edges, so this is a floor, not the full lock-file count. Edge data carries no version, so an 'outdated' breakdown isn't available.

sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.name: Documentation Discoverability
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.question: Can a newcomer find the docs?

sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.label: documentation signals present
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.unification: Fraction of four boolean signals present (README · homepage · wiki · pages).
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.notes: Four discoverability signals from the GME-extracted metadata: a README file, a homepage / documentation link, a project wiki, and a GitHub Pages site. A high score means a newcomer can find the docs without reading the source.

sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.name: License Coverage
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.question: Does the project declare a license?
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.description: Whether the repo declares an SPDX license. Per-repo it's yes/no; the project mean reads as the share of repositories with a declared license.
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.label: declared license
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.unification: 1 if ``license_spdx`` is set, else 0; project mean = coverage.
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.notes: Whether the repository declares a license (SPDX id from the GME ``license_spdx`` field). Per-repo it's yes/no; across a project the mean is the share of repositories that declare a license. Per-*file* coverage needs file-level scanning, which isn't collected — this is the repo-level signal.

sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.name: Release Frequency
sdsc-ordes/zarr-linked-data.question: How often does it ship releases?
